text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The conservative People's Party wants the Social Democrats to support a renewed candidacy of President Thomas Klestil in elections due in 1998.
- Chamber of Economy has criticised Chancellor Viktor Klima's proposal for obligatory collective agreements for flexible work hours.
- Vienna's harbour expects more trade after a cooperation agreement with Rotterdam was sigend.
- No new jobs have been created by the introduction of longer opening hours at the beginning of the year, says private employees union boss Hans Sallmutter.
- Planned job cuts at mining engineer VA Bergtechnik have been cancelled. However, 500 of the 635 employees will have to work reduced hours.
- Vienna's employment agency Arbeitsmarktservice says Vienna's industry has too few innovative jobs, as unemployment is steadily on the rise.
- Sugarmaker Agrana wants to buy salt monopoly Salinen AG, which is due to be privatised soon.
- Builder Howe Bau wants to take over builder Hazet which currently has a debt of 900 million schillings.
- Datakom, a unit of Post & Telekom Austria, has to pay a year's turnover for debts of its parent postal company.
- Employers are struggling to find a common line on flexibilisation of workhours. Meanwhile conservative Environment Minister Martin Bartenstein welcomes Klima's proposal on this issue.
- The Creditanstalt Investment Bank wants to remain part of the future Bank Austria-Creditanstalt group.
